methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: AI pressure grows on Richmond's young workforce - Axios
signals.signal_reading: Young workers facing AI displacement pressure without corresponding deep capability-building programs signals shallow anxiety without distributed skill depth, creating workforce vulnerability rather than adaptive capacity.

signals.title: EPA grant backs community-driven workforce training in Southwest Virginia - Virginia Tech News
signals.signal_reading: EPA-funded community-driven workforce training in historically underserved Southwest Virginia represents distributed capacity-building with local ownership, directly countering the concentration dynamic if implementation achieves genuine skill depth.

signals.title: Pentagon Expands Scale AI Deal to $500M and AI Defense Firm TurbineOne Moves HQ to Northern Virginia - Clearance Jobs
signals.signal_reading: Pentagon's $500M Scale AI expansion and TurbineOne HQ relocation to NoVA intensifies defense-AI capability concentration in the region, deepening technical expertise but reinforcing the metro hub gravity well that leaves other regions dependent rather than capable.

signals.title: Teaching AI by Doing, Not Studying - Inside Higher Ed
signals.signal_reading: Hands-on AI pedagogy focused on practical doing rather than theoretical study signals potential for deep, democratized capability development if implemented broadly across Virginia's educational institutions, not just elite tech programs.

signals.title: Roanoke College president: Virginia’s future workforce depends on fixing the path from college to career - Cardinal News
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College president's diagnosis of a broken college-to-career pipeline reveals structural barriers preventing workforce capability distribution even where educational institutions exist, suggesting neither depth nor breadth is materializing in non-metro regions.
